test_plan.scope: Validate FR-016 (jitter-tolerant span-based sustained confirmation) and FR-017 (bounded O(1) retention) in internal/alerts/engine.go sustainedWindow.add, plus regression NFR-005..009 (non-breach reset, gap reset, duration<=0 short-circuit, interval-aligned TC-NA-076e equivalence, no change to cooldown/dispatch) and NFR-010 (CI runs the suite).
test_plan.approach: White-box unit tests on sustainedWindow.add driven by an explicit fake clock (base 2026-05-11T10:00:00Z) — each TC constructs sustainedWindow{duration, interval} directly and calls add(ruleID, baseTime+offset, breaching), asserting the boolean return per call. add() is pure in-process logic so unit level fully covers FR-016/017 and the regression NFRs; one integration TC drives Engine cooldown to pin NFR-009. E2E is not applicable: the change has no UI/HTTP surface (declared in no_go_zone), so the e2e column is '-' for every requirement.
fixtures: base = 2026-05-11T10:00:00Z (time.Date, UTC) — all sample timestamps are base + offsetSeconds
newWindow(d, i) returns &sustainedWindow{duration: d, interval: i} with duration=60s, interval=10s unless a TC states otherwise
add(w, offsetSec, breaching) calls w.add(int64(1), base.Add(offsetSec*time.Second), breaching) and returns the bool
fakeDispatcher (integration TC only) records fire-event count, reused from the existing alerts engine test harness
test_plan.exit_criteria: FR-016 has happy+edge+negative coverage with one h and one f TC; every MUST NFR (NFR-005..010) has >=1 falsifiable TC; no TC asserts any no_go_zone behavior (no UI, no new endpoint, no schema); all timestamps are explicit; no absolute paths.

test_cases.title: Sustained breach confirms once elapsed span reaches D under jitter
preconditions: sample offsets (seconds) with jitter, each gap <= 2*interval=20s: 0, 9, 21, 29, 38, 47, 58, 63
test_cases.given: a window with D=60s, interval=10s, and breaching samples arriving with jitter at offsets 0,9,21,29,38,47,58,63s (every gap <=20s so no reset)
test_cases.when: w.add is called in sequence for each sample
test_cases.then: add returns false for offsets 0..58 (span < 60s) and returns true for the first time at offset 63 (span 63s >= 60s)
test_cases.expected_result: false on every call through offset 58; true on the call at offset 63

test_cases.title: Knife-edge: confirming sample lands after t0+D with the t0+D sample missing
preconditions: sample offsets: 0,10,20,30,40,50,57,63 (the offset-60 sample is missing due to jitter; gap 57->63 = 6s <=20s)
test_cases.given: breaching samples at offsets 0,10,20,30,40,50,57,63s — the exact pattern that the OLD cutoff-equality code never confirmed (cutoff=3s trims the offset-0 run-start, leaving samples[0] at offset 10 > cutoff)
test_cases.when: w.add is called in sequence
test_cases.then: add returns false through offset 57 (span 57s) and returns true at offset 63 (span 63s >= 60s) — the historical knife-edge failure now confirms
test_cases.expected_result: true at offset 63; would have been false under the previous implementation

test_cases.title: Boundary: exactly D confirms; single sample (span 0) does not
test_cases.given: a fresh window receives a single breaching sample at offset 0 (span 0), then interval-aligned breaching samples through offset 60
test_cases.when: w.add is called for offset 0, then 10,20,30,40,50,60
test_cases.then: add returns false at offset 0 (span 0 < 60, single sample) and at offsets 10..50; add returns true at offset 60 (span exactly 60s satisfies >= 60s inclusive boundary)
test_cases.expected_result: false at offset 0 and 10..50; true at offset 60 (>= is inclusive)

test_cases.title: Negative: span below D never confirms (no early firing)
test_cases.given: a window with D=60s receiving breaching samples whose first-to-latest span never exceeds 50s
test_cases.when: w.add is called for each of offsets 0,10,20,30,40,50
test_cases.then: add returns false on every call (span 0..50s is always < 60s) — confirmation never fires early
test_cases.expected_result: false on all six calls; no true is ever returned

test_cases.title: Bounded retention: a long continuous breach allocates zero per add
test_cases.given: an active sustained breach window (D=60s, interval=10s)
test_cases.when: testing.AllocsPerRun(1000, ...) measures 1000 consecutive breaching w.add calls advancing the timestamp by 10s each
test_cases.then: allocations-per-run is 0 (O(1) scalar state; no per-sample slice growth)
test_cases.expected_result: AllocsPerRun == 0; a slice-appending implementation reports > 0 and fails

test_cases.title: Bounded retention: state stays O(1) across 100x the duration
test_cases.given: a continuous breach lasting 100*D (6000s) at 10s intervals (600 samples)
test_cases.when: all 600 breaching samples are added in order
test_cases.then: the window's retained state does not grow with sample count (allocs remain 0 after the first call; no unbounded slice)
test_cases.expected_result: retained-state size is constant regardless of elapsed breach length

test_cases.title: Retention never drops the run-start: confirmation still fires after a very long breach
test_cases.given: 10000 consecutive breaching samples at 10s intervals (offsets 0..99990s)
test_cases.when: w.add is called for every sample in order
test_cases.then: add returns true from offset 60 onward (run-start preserved; trimming never causes a missed/reset confirmation)
test_cases.expected_result: true continuously from offset 60 to 99990; a buggy trim discarding firstAt returns false and fails

test_cases.title: After a non-breach reset, a fresh full-duration breach confirms correctly
test_cases.given: a window where breaching samples ran to offset 50, then a breaching=false sample at offset 55 reset the run
test_cases.when: breaching samples resume at offsets 60,70,...,120
test_cases.then: add returns false until offset 120 where the fresh run's span reaches 60s, then true (reset produced a clean, correct restart)
test_cases.expected_result: first true at offset 120

test_cases.title: Non-breach on an empty window is a safe no-op
test_cases.given: a fresh window with no samples yet (no active run)
test_cases.when: w.add is called with breaching=false
test_cases.then: add returns false and does not panic or create a run
test_cases.expected_result: false; no panic; window remains inactive

test_cases.title: Non-breach sample clears an active run
test_cases.given: an active breach run with breaching samples through offset 50 (span 50s)
test_cases.when: w.add(1, base+55s, false) is called, then breaching resumes at 60..115
test_cases.then: the false call returns false and clears the run; the resumed run is measured from offset 60, never confirming from stale pre-reset samples
test_cases.expected_result: false at 55; first true at 120 (fresh run)

test_cases.title: Gap of exactly 2*interval does NOT reset the run (boundary)
test_cases.given: an active run with samples at 0,10,20,30,40 and the next breaching sample at offset 60 (gap 20s == 2*interval, not greater)
test_cases.when: w.add is called for the offset-60 sample and breaching continues
test_cases.then: the run is NOT reset (gap is not > 2*interval); span is measured from offset 0, so add returns true at offset 60 (span 60s)
test_cases.expected_result: true at offset 60; run preserved across the boundary gap

test_cases.title: Gap just over 2*interval resets the run
test_cases.given: an active run with samples at 0,10,20,30,40,50 and the next breaching sample at offset 71 (gap 21s > 2*interval=20s)
test_cases.when: w.add is called for the offset-71 sample
test_cases.then: the run resets (reason=sample_gap) and restarts at offset 71
test_cases.expected_result: add returns false at 71; run restarted

test_cases.title: After a gap reset, stale samples never confirm early
test_cases.given: an active run through offset 50, then a breaching sample at offset 75 (gap 25s > 20s)
test_cases.when: the offset-75 sample resets the run; breaching continues at 85,95,...,135
test_cases.then: add returns false at 75 and first returns true at offset 135 (span from 75 reaches 60s) — not from stale pre-gap samples
test_cases.expected_result: false at 75; first true at 135

test_cases.title: duration == 0 returns breaching=true verbatim
test_cases.given: a window with duration=0, interval=10s
test_cases.when: w.add(1, anyTime, true) is called
test_cases.then: add returns true immediately, with no sustained gating and no state mutation
test_cases.expected_result: true; identical to an instantaneous threshold

test_cases.title: negative duration also short-circuits to the breaching flag
test_cases.given: a window with duration=-5s, interval=10s
test_cases.when: w.add is called with breaching=true then breaching=false
test_cases.then: add returns true then false, mirroring the breaching argument regardless of the negative duration
test_cases.expected_result: true then false; negative duration handled like zero

test_cases.title: duration == 0 returns breaching=false verbatim
test_cases.given: a window with duration=0, interval=10s
test_cases.when: w.add(1, anyTime, false) is called
test_cases.then: add returns false immediately without creating a sustained run
test_cases.expected_result: false; no gating applied

test_cases.title: Interval-aligned confirmation (TC-NA-076e equivalent) still passes
test_cases.given: perfectly interval-aligned breaching samples at offsets 0,10,20,30,40,50,60 (D=60s)
test_cases.when: w.add is called for offsets 0..60
test_cases.then: add returns false at 0..50 and true at offset 60 — identical to the pre-existing TC-NA-076e expectation
test_cases.expected_result: true at offset 60; aligned case preserved

test_cases.title: Aligned breach keeps confirming on the sample after D
test_cases.given: aligned breaching samples through offset 60 (already confirmed) plus one more at offset 70
test_cases.when: w.add is called for the offset-70 sample
test_cases.then: add continues to return true at offset 70 (span 70s >= 60s); confirmation is stable past D
test_cases.expected_result: true at offset 70

test_cases.title: Aligned breach below D does not confirm
test_cases.given: aligned breaching samples at offsets 0,10,20,30,40,50 only (span 50s < 60s)
test_cases.when: w.add is called for offsets 0..50
test_cases.then: add returns false on every call (aligned but insufficient span)
test_cases.expected_result: false on all calls; no early confirmation

test_cases.title: Confirmed sustained breach fires exactly once on confirmation
test_cases.given: Engine + fakeDispatcher + fakeClock (10s ticks); one rule sustained_duration=60s cooldown=15m, breached every tick
test_cases.when: the engine evaluates from 10:00:00Z until just after the 60s span confirms
test_cases.then: exactly 1 fire event is dispatched at/after the confirming tick
test_cases.expected_result: fakeDispatcher fire count == 1 at confirmation

test_cases.title: Continuing breach fires again only after the cooldown elapses
test_cases.given: the same rule breached continuously for 20 minutes after confirmation (cooldown 15m)
test_cases.when: the engine evaluates every 10s through 10:20:00Z
test_cases.then: exactly 2 fire events occur: first at confirmation, second at/after cooldown expiry — unchanged cooldown behavior
test_cases.expected_result: fire count == 2; second fire >= 15m after first

test_cases.title: No duplicate fire inside the cooldown window
test_cases.given: a confirmed breach with cooldown=15m, continuously breaching
test_cases.when: the engine evaluates repeatedly within the 15-minute window after the first fire
test_cases.then: no additional fire event is dispatched before the cooldown expires (dedup/cooldown unchanged)
test_cases.expected_result: fire count stays 1 throughout the cooldown window

test_cases.title: Push to main runs the full Go test suite
test_cases.given: the CI workflow configured for the repository
test_cases.when: a push to the main branch triggers the pipeline
test_cases.then: the CI job executes go test ./... and completes the alerts package tests
test_cases.expected_result: go test ./... runs on push to main

test_cases.title: The alerts package (TC-SAW-*) is included in the CI run
test_cases.given: the CI test command go test ./...
test_cases.when: the suite is enumerated
test_cases.then: internal/alerts/... is included so every TC-SAW-* unit/integration test executes in CI
test_cases.expected_result: alerts package tests are part of the CI run

test_cases.title: A failing alerts test fails the CI job
test_cases.given: a deliberately failing TC-SAW-* test (simulated)
test_cases.when: the CI pipeline runs go test ./...
test_cases.then: the job exits non-zero and is marked failed (the bug cannot be merged silently)
test_cases.expected_result: non-zero exit; CI job fails
